definitions.explanation: A slightly casual way of saying 'once' or 'one time,' more colloquial than 一度 or 一回. Particularly common in Kansai dialect but widely understood throughout Japan.

definitions.gloss: all at once; in one go
definitions.explanation: Used in the pattern 一遍に to mean doing something all at once rather than in stages or portions, such as carrying everything in a single trip or eating all the food at the same time.

examples.japanese: {一遍|いっぺん}{会|あ}ったことがある。
{一遍|いっぺん}でいいから{本場|ほんば}のピザを{食|た}べてみたい。
examples.english: I'd like to try authentic pizza just once.

examples.japanese: {一遍|いっぺん}に{片付|かたづ}けよう。
examples.english: Let's take care of it all at once.

examples.japanese: そんなに{一遍|いっぺん}に{食|た}べたらお{腹|なか}を{壊|こわ}すよ。
examples.english: If you eat that much all at once, you'll upset your stomach.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}を{一遍|いっぺん}に{運|はこ}ぶのは{無理|むり}だ。
examples.english: It's impossible to carry the luggage all in one go.

notes:
A slightly casual adverb meaning "once" or "all at once." More colloquial than {一度|いちど} or {一回|いっかい}. Particularly common in Kansai dialect but widely understood across Japan. Sense 2 ({一遍|いっぺん}に) means doing something all at once rather than in stages.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一遍|いっぺん} + verb: once; one time (sense 1)
- {一遍|いっぺん}に: all at once; in one go (sense 2)
- {一遍|いっぺん}でいいから: just once (emphatic wish)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一度|いちど} — once (standard, slightly more formal)
- {一回|いっかい} — one time (neutral, most common)
- {一気|いっき}に — in one breath; at a stretch (emphasizes speed/intensity more than {一遍|いっぺん}に)

NOTE:
Do not confuse with the homophone {一変|いっぺん} (complete change), which has a completely different meaning.
